assumptions: Finite simple two-prefix split graphs; triangle packing is edge-disjoint and every core edge has one shared capacity.
Q has integral core-triangle variables but fractional leaf allocations; J and nu are different parameters.
The main new all-order construction requires affine-compatible core and prefix sizes. Its dimension and repetitions may grow; constants are explicit.
The universal proof uses elementary finite vector arithmetic, exact capacity counting and LP weak duality, not an external design-existence theorem.

atomic_claims.text: For r>=3 in the capped domain, an optimal full dual with positive prices only 1/3 implies L=(C(r,2)+ap+bq)/3; actual objective loss is exactly one third of unused core and tagged endpoint capacities.

For r,a,b compatible powers of three (or empty prefixes) and p<=a-1, p+q<=b-1 with stated zero conventions, explicit shared affine-line allocation proves L-Q<=[a(p mod 2)+b(q mod 2)]/3. Equal prefixes have the sharper d((p+q) mod 2)/3 bound.

For r=3^(2h), h>=2, a=9,b=r,p=2,q=(r-1)/2, a prefix-preserving nonlinear shear and complete reselection remove at least r(r-9)/36 old integral core triangles at zero objective loss. No reopening budget is imposed.
The new (7,3,7,1,1) full-face extreme point has value 31/3, all 31 rows saturated, and 28 positive columns of rank 28, including denominator 12. Its Q optimum is not claimed.
Uniform-face instances obtained by deleting at most two core vertices from a compatible affine host admit the specified Q witness with L-Q<=8r. This is not an arbitrary-size padding theorem.

Actual generator-side exact replays cover 939 affine parameter representations through r=27, eight named larger cases, 149 capped tuples through r=4 with Q computed on the 72 all-row uniform-face members, the named rank certificate, three deletion witnesses and twelve mutations.

objective: Attack only the full one-third optimal-dual face. Prove an explicit affine-flag subclass bound L-Q<=(a+b)/3, support-independent zero-loss global repacking and bounded deletion extension; retain arbitrary-size face and both admitted stronger obligations as open.
risks: The arbitrary-size one-third face theorem L-Q<=Kr remains unproved, as do nonuniform prices, many levels, exact split domination and the ProblemContract root.
The old quarter-valued C25 point is outside this face; the new twelfth-valued point is on it but no Q optimum is computed there.
Zero-loss large support changes are an explicit permitted global exchange, not a proof that an analogous exchange exists for every input.
